$$0 = M_0 < M_1 < M_2 < \cdots$$
and define $x_n = \tfrac{1}{j}$ for $M_{j-1} < n \le M_j$. Since each block is finite and $M_j \to \infty$, every positive integer lies in exactly one block, and $x_n = 1/j(n) \to 0$; moreover $x_n$ is non-increasing.

Let $T_n = \sum_{k=1}^n \lambda_k x_k$ denote the partial sums of the weighted series, and $B_j = S_{M_j} - S_{M_{j-1}} = \sum_{k=M_{j-1}+1}^{M_j} \lambda_k$ the sum over block $j$.

$$|S_{M_j}| \;\ge\; j\bigl(|T_{M_{j-1}}| + j + 1\bigr) + |S_{M_{j-1}}|.$$
By the reverse triangle inequality this gives
$$|B_j| = |S_{M_j} - S_{M_{j-1}}| \;\ge\; |S_{M_j}| - |S_{M_{j-1}}| \;\ge\; j\bigl(|T_{M_{j-1}}| + j + 1\bigr). \tag{$\ast$}$$

Since $x_k = 1/j$ is constant on block $j$,
$$T_{M_j} \;=\; T_{M_{j-1}} + \tfrac{1}{j}\,B_j.$$
Applying $(\ast)$ and the triangle inequality,
$$|T_{M_j}| \;\ge\; \tfrac{1}{j}|B_j| - |T_{M_{j-1}}| \;\ge\; \bigl(|T_{M_{j-1}}| + j + 1\bigr) - |T_{M_{j-1}}| \;=\; j + 1.$$

**Conclusion of the induction.** For every $j \ge 1$,
$$|T_{M_j}| \;\ge\; j + 1 \;\longrightarrow\; \infty.$$
Thus the subsequence $(T_{M_j})$ of partial sums of $\sum \lambda_n x_n$ escapes to infinity in modulus, so $(T_n)$ cannot converge to any finite limit. Hence $\sum \lambda_n x_n$ **diverges**.

Meanwhile $x_n = 1/j(n) \to 0$, and the sequence is non-increasing (real, positive). Therefore we have produced a sequence $x_n \to 0$ — in fact monotone non-increasing, matching the strongest form of Dirichlet's hypothesis — for which $\sum \lambda_n x_n$ diverges.

Hence the converse of Dirichlet's test **is true**: unboundedness of the partial sums $\sum_{k=1}^n \lambda_k$ is both sufficient and necessary for the existence of a null sequence $x_n$ making $\sum \lambda_n x_n$ diverge.
